Plompy Local 0.13.0Source guide · 2026-11-12

Documentation/Compatibility and verification

What has been verified

These pages describe Plompy Local 0.13.0. The release provides separate core and browser images plus a downloadable starter kit. The older v0.12.0 Discord image does not contain Local mode. A container release does not establish that your model account or third-party API credentials work.

Version boundaries#

ComponentContract
Local runtimeNode 26.13.0 or newer Node 26
MCP SDKPinned by packages/local-mcp/package-lock.json
Docker0.13.0-local and 0.13.0-local-browser, Linux amd64 and arm64
Host clientsCodex and Claude Code export; explicit OpenCode V1 or V2 config
Local inferenceOllama configuration guide, not tested in this acceptance run
Existing engine OpenCode runnerIndependently pinned to 1.19.5
BrowserPinned optional Playwright dependency, sandbox enabled
Separate Discord engine image0.13.0, Codex runner inside the engine

Verification levels#

  • Offline: synthetic credentials, local fixtures and controlled responses. This can verify validation and error handling without proving vendor access.
  • Container: the actual built image starts, authenticates an MCP client and performs the checked local operations.
  • Real browser: Chromium runs inside the browser image and reads a controlled fixture with sandboxing enabled.
  • Real OpenCode client: the actual client discovers or calls the gateway. A deterministic model fixture is not a real model-provider acceptance test.
  • Live provider: an explicitly authorized call to a real account succeeds. Record provider, tool, date and outcome without secrets.

Acceptance record#

The following checks were completed on 12 November 2026. The test sources and reproducible commands are in the local MCP test guide.

CheckResult and boundary
Core and browser Docker imagesBoth source targets built successfully and ran the recorded acceptance checks. Release images and architectures are verified separately by the release workflow.
Real sandboxed browserChromium ran as UID 1000 with no sandbox-disabling flag. It read JavaScript-rendered contacts, retained the final source URL, and blocked POST and metadata requests.
Actual Codex 0.159.2 clientAn isolated client parsed the generated TOML and completed plompy_status against Docker. A deterministic local Responses mock handled two model requests; a completed MCP tool event was asserted.
Actual Claude Code 2.1.197 clientAn isolated client completed an authenticated MCP connection health check and reported Connected. No Claude agent/model turn was run.
Actual OpenCode 1.19.5 clientAn isolated client completed eight real MCP calls against Docker for a synthetic research task. A deterministic local mock model directed the calls.
Research artifactsThree controlled source pages produced two deduplicated company records, draft content, JSON and CSV. Stored files and formula-safe CSV were checked.
Container restartConfiguration, gateway token and exact artifact bytes persisted across a real restart.
Public OpenAI DocsReal remote initialization and search_openai_docs with query API Responses and limit 1 succeeded at 15:31 UTC. No model account or paid inference was used.
Other paid API providersNot live-tested with account credentials. Offline validation does not prove provider access.
OpenCode V2Configuration generation is supported; the V2 client was not exercised in the recorded acceptance run.
OllamaDocumented setup only. Ollama and local-model quality were not tested, and no model was downloaded.

A configuration export or CLI registration alone must not be described as a completed model-powered task. The Codex and OpenCode checks used actual clients with controlled model fixtures; the Claude Code check covered authenticated server connectivity only.

The synthetic research test proves client transport, tool execution, rendering and persistence. It does not prove live search-provider coverage, paid model reasoning quality, mailbox access or email deliverability. Third-party integration failures remain possible because of authentication, plan limits, changed tool names or service availability.

Deliberate first-version limits#

  • No email sending, mailbox integration or bulk outreach.
  • No nested agent or model inside the gateway.
  • No automatic import of host credentials or browser profiles.
  • No vendor OAuth implementation in the gateway.
  • No Camoufox Docker support in this profile.
  • No TinyFish autonomous task tool in the research profile.
  • No arbitrary custom MCP servers in the local research profile.
  • No generic shell, arbitrary browser script or unrestricted tool-invocation endpoint.
  • Documentation content is English; the existing landing retains English and Polish routes.
